issues.legal_issue: Acquisition by the State of proprietary interests in a village does not extinguish a co-sharer’s right to establish the extent of their pre-existing share for claims to compensation and home-farm land.
material_facts: The suit sought a declaration of a share in the village and partition of the property attributable to that share.
The State had acquired the village’s proprietary interests, but home-farm land was not acquired under the Act.
The lower courts had found that the claimant was entitled to a share, although the precise extent was disputed.
issues.conclusion: The acquisition did not prevent a co-sharer from obtaining a civil-court declaration of the fact and extent of their pre-existing share, which could support a proportionate claim to compensation and home-farm land.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 4(2) of the Madhya Pradesh Abolition of Proprietary Rights (Estates, Mahals, Alienated Lands) Act, 1950 acquire proprietary rights subject to the Act and preserve possession of home-farm land. The acquisition of proprietary interests does not take away every other right a person has as an owner of property; a co-sharer may establish their share in the pre-existing proprietary rights to claim proportionate compensation and home-farm land.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_dismissal_of_share_cla: A civil appeal challenges the dismissal of a claim to establish a share in village property.
predicates.state_acquired_village_proprietary_inter: The State acquired the proprietary interests in the village.
predicates.claimant_seeks_declaration_of_preexistin: A claimant asks a civil court to declare the extent of their share in the village’s pre-existing proprietary interests.
predicates.home_farm_land_not_acquired: The land claimed as home-farm land was not acquired by the State.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal concerns dismissal of a share claim, the State has acquired the village’s proprietary interests, the claimant seeks a declaration of a pre-existing share, and home-farm land was not acquired, the claimant may establish the share for proportionate compensation and home-farm claims.

issues.legal_issue: The right to seek partition of home-farm land in an undivided village is not defeated because the claimant was not personally cultivating the land.
material_facts: The village remained undivided, and the co-sharers’ use or allocation of land was tentative and subject to partition.
The claimant was not personally in cultivating possession of land in the village.
Land was in the cultivating possession of co-sharers and also in the possession of lessees or ordinary tenants.
The claim included partition of land that qualified as home-farm land.
issues.conclusion: A co-sharer could enforce a claim to partition home-farm land, and that right was not affected by the Act; land cultivated by a co-sharer, or held by a lessee or ordinary tenant, was treated as being in the possession of the undivided body of co-sharers.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(g)(iii) of the Act defines home-farm land in Berar to include land under a superior holder’s personal cultivation, land held by a lessee, and land held by an ordinary tenant, while excluding specified categories of tenants. Section 4(2) preserves possession of home-farm land. Where a village remains undivided, land in the cultivating possession of a co-sharer, or in the possession of a lessee or ordinary tenant, is deemed to be in the possession of the body of co-sharers, and the Act does not bar partition. The Court distinguished Chhote Khan v. Mohammad Obedullakhan and referred to Rahmatullah Khan v. Mahabirsingh.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_dismissal_of_partition: A civil appeal challenges the dismissal of a claim to partition village land.
predicates.village_undivided: The village has not been partitioned among its co-sharers.
predicates.claimant_is_co_sharer: The claimant holds a share in the village property.
predicates.land_is_home_farm: The land at issue falls within the category of home-farm land retained by its owners.
predicates.land_held_by_co_sharer_lessee_or_ordinar: The land is in the cultivating possession of a co-sharer or is held by a lessee or ordinary tenant.

issues.definition: If a partition claim concerns home-farm land in an undivided village, the claimant is a co-sharer, and the land is held by a co-sharer, lessee, or ordinary tenant, the claimant may enforce partition.

issues.legal_issue: A suit concerning individual property rights and land not vested in the State cannot be dismissed in its entirety merely because a claim to possession of other property would depend on a former proprietor’s status.
material_facts: The suit sought several forms of relief, including partition of home-farm land that had not vested in the State.
The High Court dismissed the suit as infructuous on the basis that the Act vested proprietary interests in the State.
The High Court relied on Chhote Khan, which concerned an ex-lambardar’s claim, based on that office, to possession of abadi land vested in the State.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in dismissing the suit as wholly infructuous; the appeals were allowed, the High Court decrees were set aside, and the suit was remitted for decision on its merits.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished a suit brought by a former proprietor in that capacity for possession of property vested in the State from a suit based on individual rights independent of that status. Chhote Khan v. Mohammad Obedullakhan concerned the former kind of claim and did not justify dismissing a suit that included claims concerning property not vested in the State. The distinction was also discussed in Rahmatullah Khan v. Mahabirsingh.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_whole_suit_dismissal_a: A civil appeal challenges an order dismissing an entire suit as having become infructuous.
predicates.suit_includes_claims_to_property_not_ves: The suit includes claims concerning property that did not vest in the State.
predicates.claims_based_on_individual_rights_indepe: The claims rest on individual property rights that do not depend on the claimant’s status as a former proprietor.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges dismissal of an entire suit as infructuous, the suit includes claims to property not vested in the State, and those claims rest on individual rights independent of former-proprietor status, the suit cannot be dismissed as wholly infructuous.
